In full, the address on the state of the nation by the Prime Minister, Christophe Marie Joseph Dabire, on Thursday 16 May 2019

Mr President, Honourable Deputies, Ladies and Gentlemen,

On 18 February, you did me the honour of receiving me on the occasion of the presentation of my General Policy Statement, at the end of which you granted me your confidence for the conduct of government action.

On this day, 16 May 2019, I once again have the honour and the privilege of appearing before you to set out for you the State of the Nation in accordance with the provisions of Article 109 of our constitution.

Through this exercise, it is my pleasure to render account to your august Assembly of the state of the nation, so that you may be aware of the achievements of government action, but also so that you may become conscious of the challenges to be met and of the prospects relating to the implementation of public policies.

The government's action aims to carry out the programme of the President of Faso, His Excellency Mr Roch Marc Christian KABORE, whose vision is "To build, with the people, a Burkina Faso of democracy, of economic and social progress, of freedom and of justice." This programme has been set out in a National Economic and Social Development Plan (PNDES), whose operationalisation is carried out through sectoral and territorial planning instruments.

Mr President, Ladies and Gentlemen Deputies,

It was in a particularly difficult national context that the government's action was conducted during the year 2018 by my predecessor Mr Paul Kaba THIEBA, whose patriotic commitment I salute. It was, as we all experienced, a year in which the security of property and persons was severely tested. Indeed, during the year 2018, our country experienced numerous terrorist attacks that caused several victims. To these barbaric acts, which I condemn forcefully, are added recurrent hostage-takings involving both national and foreign figures.

Terrorism, beyond attacks on the symbols of the State, has implemented its strategy of divide and rule by means of community conflicts of an ethnic character and through targeted attacks on religious buildings and gatherings. We have clearly perceived this project of destabilising the country by provoking chaos. But we are not going to give up, nor close our eyes before the unfolding of so disastrous a design.

I should like, at this solemn moment, to salute the memory of all those who have fallen, victims of terrorism and of community clashes. At the same time, I wish to express all my admiration for, and to encourage, the agents of the devolved administration and of the local authorities who have remained at their posts to ensure the continuity of public service and the presence of the State in difficult areas.

Honourable Deputies,

The year 2018 was also marked by numerous social disturbances which affected the effectiveness of public action. The demonstrations often fell within the law or sometimes took more pernicious forms. I understand the impatience of workers, especially in the public sector, because in the history of Burkina Faso the State has made commitments that have suffered in their implementation, thereby provoking a climate of mistrust and sometimes of defiance towards authority.

In this context of social ferment which has hardened, the government, on the instructions of the President of Faso and faithful to its commitments, has remained constant in its approach of favouring consultations as well as negotiations in order to clear the backlog and to consider the future serenely.

Indeed, in his Address to the Nation of 31 December 2017, the President of Faso had announced that the government would undertake a reform of the remuneration system, in consultation with the social partners and the other components of the Nation, in order to give rise to a modern, dynamic civil service, turned towards development and at the exclusive service of the users of the public service.

The political will of the Head of State, guided by the principles of justice and equity, materialised in the holding, from 12 to 14 June 2018, of the national conference on the remuneration system of public State agents, which brought together the vital forces of the nation. At its conclusion, committees were set up to implement and monitor the recommendations resulting from the proceedings.

I measure the scale of the expectations of public agents as well as of our compatriots, and I should like to reassure everyone that the government's quest, through these efforts, is to preserve social peace by repairing the often serious injustices between workers having the same level of qualification and, at times, within the same corps.

I reiterate the Head of State's call for a social truce, launched on 31 December 2018, with a view to creating a climate of serenity favourable to the implementation of the various reforms undertaken. The government seeks the improvement of the well-being of all Burkinabe without any exclusion, and it is only social justice that each actor should make concessions in the national interest.

That is why I solemnly invite all the components of our society to unity so that, all together, beyond our legitimate differences, we may achieve the common objective of the prosperity of Burkina Faso, which alone can justify any commitment. Mr President, Honourable Deputies,

Despite the adversities I have just mentioned, the government has not failed in its essential missions, which are to:

1) preserve the integrity of the territory and national unity; and 2) ensure the progress of our country on the path of consolidating the fundamental values of freedom, democracy, justice and human rights.

Last year's difficult context has likewise not hindered the achievement of the objective of creating wealth with a view to improving the living conditions of the Burkinabe.

Building on the major achievements in matters of governance, of the invigoration of economic activity and of access to basic social services by the whole population, it seemed to me logical to insist on three essential points, namely: 1) reforming institutions and modernising the administration; 2) developing human capital; and finally 3) energising the sectors that drive the economy and jobs.

I should also like to recall that my intention is not to present a detailed record of government action, but to highlight the most salient aspects of the state of the nation. The details are contained in the annex document that has been transmitted to you.

Mr President, Ladies and Gentlemen Deputies,

Reforming institutions and modernising the State for more security, justice, democracy and freedom has been the compass of government action in recent years. Reform with a view to modernising and adapting to the evolution of the times is an obligation for a nation concerned to guarantee its youth a bright future. In this respect the government has pursued four major objectives: 1) promoting the security of property and persons; 2) improving political and administrative governance as well as the management of the national economy; 3) strengthening decentralisation; and finally 4) energising local economies with a view to reducing regional development disparities.

History has never been that tranquil course of the evolution of societies or nations. It is often made of tremors, turbulence, even dramas which sometimes reveal a disturbing disorder in the order of society. It provides lessons and calls for vigilance, for combined efforts to forge the national destiny. Terrorism, which a few years ago appeared as a threat at our borders, is today a brutal and cruel reality weaving its web throughout the country and in other spaces which, I am convinced, entertained the illusion of security.

The terrorist strikes have changed our priorities without making us renounce our objectives. We have had to strengthen the operational and organisational capacities of our national armed forces and our internal security forces. We have had to intensify territorial security operations, at the end of which the armed forces, thanks to their capacity for resilience, have fortunately neutralised terrorist groups which have plunged, and still too frequently plunge, our nation into mourning. They have also arrested numerous suspects following large-scale sweep operations carried out in crime-prone areas. This is the place for me to pay vibrant tribute to all our national armed forces and to our internal security forces for the difficult combat they are waging against barbarity.

Contrary to a certain opinion which takes us to task in this tireless struggle against terrorism, I should like to recall that our national armed forces and our internal security forces operate within a framework governed by law. And our country respects, and intends to respect, all the conventions it has signed in matters of human rights. That is why, since the outbreak of the phenomenon of violent extremism in West Africa, we have proved our legendary hospitality by welcoming tens of thousands of refugees. Our country still today hosts more than 25,000 refugees and records nearly 5,000 asylum seekers as well as about 150,000 internally displaced persons owing to insecurity and community conflicts. We treat refugees and displaced persons who have come from abroad in accordance with the international conventions relating to refugees and stateless persons.

As regards the particular case of internally displaced persons, they are received and protected in the reception sites of the Sahel, Centre-North, North, East and Centre regions in accordance with the international conventions relating to the protection of and assistance to internally displaced persons.

Looking ahead, the government will pursue its efforts to equip the units of our armed forces and paramilitary forces with strategic and specific means, will ensure their training, will increase their numbers, and will finally strengthen and pool information systems thanks to partnership with the countries of the sub-region and with friendly countries outside Africa.

Burkina Faso intends to pursue its efforts to ensure its standing on the international stage. This means playing its role by taking an active part in the process of regional and sub-regional integration and forging relations beneficial to the development of our economy and the flourishing of our people. It is on the strength of this vision that His Excellency the President of Faso chose the China of Beijing in order to forge a win-win partnership. The Ouagadougou-Beijing axis is promising in terms of the realisation of national and sub-regional infrastructure.

The fight against terrorism has allowed us to appreciate the solidity of our ties of cooperation with France and the European Union, which accompany our strategy of response to violent extremism and take part in financing our development. The recent state visit of German Chancellor Angela Merkel gave rise to a G5 Sahel summit and constitutes an important step in the strengthening of our cooperative relations.

Likewise, the Ouagadougou-Washington axis is being consolidated with Burkina Faso's eligibility in December 2016 for a second Millennium Challenge Corporation (MCC) Compact and its eligibility in December 2018 for the regional Compact. The feasibility studies are nearing completion, which attests to the confidence our American partners place in us.

Our diplomatic standing is also measured by our capacity to attract financing for the benefit of our economy. In 2018, we signed 88 agreements for an amount of 1,176 billion FCFA. It is also measured by the election of His Excellency the President of Faso to the head of the G5 Sahel, supported by the international community, by the numerous accreditations of chancelleries in our country and by the visits carried out by the President of Faso notably in Europe, the Near East and China.

Mr President, Ladies and Gentlemen Deputies,

Over the past year, the government has worked to consolidate good political and administrative governance, that is to say, to promote democracy, human rights and justice, and to modernise the public administration.

I welcome the smooth conduct of the trial of the coup attempt of 16 September 2015, begun on 27 February 2018 and still ongoing. Every democrat can rejoice at the stage reached in this judgment, for many people were sceptical as to whether it would be held and as to the court's capacity to conduct the case. Since the time of justice is not that of men, still less that of politicians, the government, respectful of the sacrosanct principle of the separation of powers, strongly encourages the judiciary to assume its responsibilities so that justice remains an instrument that strengthens national unity and preserves social peace.

Beyond the holding of this trial, the government has also consolidated the performance of justice, both from the point of view of its technical and operational capacities and of its accessibility, geographical as well as financial, through the judicial assistance fund.

Moreover, the specialisation of justice is under way. Indeed, after their establishment in 2017, the specialised judicial poles for the fight against economic and financial offences judged 12 cases and registered 125 files in 2018.

With regard to the particular case of the Yirgou tragedy, the investigations have progressed on the ground, and the government remains attentive to the requests of the judicial actors in charge of handling this case, providing them with the necessary logistical and financial support.

To date, the procedure is following its course with more than 160 persons heard. Moreover, the preliminary investigation relating to the terrorist attack that led to the death of the village chief and his companions has been concluded.

On the legislative front, the adoption in May 2018 of the penal code, which introduces advances in the functioning of the judicial system, is a guarantee of improved sanctions and of strengthened respect for human rights.

Significant efforts have been deployed in order to promote prison activities that prepare detainees for professional and social reintegration. Certain detention and correctional houses have been brought up to standard, with the aim of improving detention conditions.

Alongside justice, notable progress has been recorded in the effective establishment of the branches of the National Observatory for the Prevention and Management of Community Conflicts. The operationalisation of this powerful tool of prevention and promotion of peace should make it possible to prevent inter-community conflicts such as those that have made national headlines.

Good political and administrative governance implies modernising the public administration in order to make it effective in the accomplishment of the sovereign missions of the State. Through the modernisation of the administration we pursue the objectives of improving its functioning, strengthening its effectiveness and the quality of public management, and finally improving its performance in order to break with routine practices and red tape, a source of slowness in the handling of files.

In the process of modernising the public administration, we attach capital importance to the digital transition, which offers infinite possibilities for the processing and management of files. It is on the strength of this orientation that we have committed ourselves to promoting e-governance and to improving the recruitment process for civil service agents through the e-competition platform. Indeed, the virtual one-stop window platform of the public administration was launched in 2018. This window allows the citizen to access directly online the information, procedures, forms and services of the public administration. To date, more than 500 administrative procedures of Ministries and Institutions are listed there.

Political and administrative governance also consists in working to fight bad practices and deviations with regard to deontology and ethics. The special review on the state of implementation of the recommendations of the ASCE/LC, organised by the monitoring committee within the Prime Minister's Office, noted that some fifty audit and investigation reports carried out in 2018 by the ASCE/LC were officially transmitted for my attention. With a view to strengthening the actions to fight fraud and corruption, all the recommendations made were addressed to the ministerial departments concerned. In particular, I have instructed the government to revisit procedures, to strengthen internal control and to energise disciplinary boards, in order to eradicate the scourges that undermine the functioning of our administration.

Moreover, the government is working to improve the ASCE/LC's missions in matters of investigating cases, in order to allow it to play fully its role as judicial police officer. Mr President, Ladies and

Gentlemen Deputies,

Citizens' access to information is an inalienable right in contemporary democracies. On this subject, Madam Audrey Azoulay, Director-General of UNESCO, rightly said, and I quote: "Every State governed by the rule of law, respectful of individual freedoms, in particular the freedoms of opinion, conscience and expression, rests on a free, independent press, sheltered from all censorship and all coercion." This assertion translates the government's intimate conviction to promote a plural and professional press whose responsibility constantly increases. The significant progress achieved in promoting press freedom has earned our country a ranking, according to Reporters Without Borders, of 36th in the world out of 180 countries and 4th in Africa in terms of press freedom. According to this ranking, it occupies first place among French-speaking African countries.

The government congratulates all the actors who have worked for such a performance. It intends to stay the course by working to strengthen the contribution of the media to the consolidation of the rule of law and of national unity.

To this end, citizens' accessibility to the media has been increased thanks to the installation of 35 Digital Terrestrial Television (DTT) broadcasting stations, of which 29 are operational, to the strengthening of the technical facilities of National Television and of Editions Sidwaya with various equipment and technical tools, and to the granting of a subsidy of 400 million to 96 press companies.

Moreover, a credit line has been opened in a local bank and endowed with an amount of 667 million FCFA to finance press companies wishing to make investments. The government remains open to all discussions aimed at pursuing the revision of the various laws so as to rid them of all the shortcomings that could hamper the activity of the media. At the same time, it will work to ensure that the information broadcast is fair and transparent so as to prevent disinformation and the dissemination of false information from harming public order and human dignity.

Mr President, Ladies and Gentlemen Deputies,

ECONOMIC GOVERNANCE

Improving the governance of our economy constituted the second major component of our policy of reforming institutions and modernising the administration.

In this field, the recovery of economic activity that we have observed since 2016 strengthened in 2018. The economic growth rate came out at 6.6% against 6.3% in 2017; 5.9% in 2016 and 3.9% in 2015. Admittedly, the progress observed is modest, but it is revealing of our capacity for resilience, which allows us to maintain a fairly stable macroeconomic environment characterised by well-controlled inflation (2% at the end of 2018), a controlled budget deficit (4.7% of GDP in 2018) and a low debt ratio (38.4% of GDP in 2018).

Hope for a better tomorrow is permitted since the public investment rate rose from 8% in 2017 to 10% of GDP in 2018, but we need stability to strengthen this trend.

The government will firmly pursue the actions that carry growth strong and sustained enough to favour the development of the private sector and consequently the creation of jobs.

Mr President, Ladies and Gentlemen Deputies,

The broadly positive evolution of the main macroeconomic indicators of our country testifies to the government's capacity to steer the national economy and to ensure the profitability of investments. We now have on this subject frameworks for a more effective steering of the national economy. These are law No. 034-2018 of 27 July 2018 concerning the steering and management of development, which strengthens the coherence of the national planning system and allows public policies to generate more intensely the expected impacts. There is also law No. 024-2018 of 28 May 2018 on orientation regarding land-use planning and sustainable territorial development in Burkina Faso, which proceeds from the need to ensure at once the spatial coherence of investments, the optimal exploitation of space and harmony in the development of the territory.

Finally, there is the National Strategy for the Promotion of Growth Poles, together with an Action Plan, which serves as a compass for the establishment of the various growth and competitiveness poles.

Still in connection with the harmonious development of the national territory, the design and beginning of implementation of the instruments for reducing regional disparities and energising local economies, namely the Emergency Programme for the Sahel in Burkina Faso (PUS-BF) and the Local Economies Development Support Programme (PADEL), also constitute genuine achievements.

Through the Emergency Programme for the Sahel in Burkina Faso, a total of 154 investment projects, worth 111 billion CFA francs in the socio-economic, governance and security fields, were executed, for the most part entirely, in 2018.

In application of the recommendation formulated by your august Assembly sitting in extraordinary session on 12 September 2018 on the security situation, the government is working to extend this programme to the various regions affected by violent extremism.

As for the Local Economies Development Support Programme (PADEL), whose objective is to fight poverty, it has already made it possible, in the Sahel region, to invest a total amount of about 3 billion CFA francs in favour of 797 promoters of informal production units, to build socio-economic infrastructure and to finance 617 micro-enterprises promoted by women and young people.

This programme, executed in the Sahel, was extended in 2018 to the following 6 regions: the East, the Centre-North, the Centre-East, the Boucle du Mouhoun, the Centre-South and the North. It will be deployed in 2019 in the six other remaining regions.

Mr President, Ladies and Gentlemen Deputies,

All these actions in favour of reducing spatial disparities in terms of economic progress are complemented by a strong will on the part of the government to promote good local governance and to strengthen decentralisation. It is in this sense that one must understand the efforts to renew the legislative and orientation frameworks of decentralisation, through the prospective vision of decentralisation towards 2040 and the national decentralisation policy together with its ten-year strategy.

These new frameworks introduce major innovations that will allow the decentralisation process: 1) to improve local authorities' access to public-private partnership financing, to conventional borrowing and to diaspora financing; 2) to broaden the base of local taxation and shared taxation to new State taxes and levies; 3) finally, to reform the public procurement regulations specific to local authorities in order to ensure speed in the awarding of public contracts within them.

The will to create an environment favourable to the emergence of a dynamic private sector has led the government to act on the lever of legislation to favour the financing of investment through: 1) the operationalisation of the new mechanism for monitoring the improvement of the business climate in order to improve Burkina Faso's rank in the Doing Business classification;

2) the creation of the Burkinabe Investment Agency (ABI) in May 2018 to replace the Investment Promotion Agency of Burkina Faso (API-BF), with the aim of instituting a suitable organisational framework capable of attracting the maximum of national and foreign direct investment to Burkina Faso; 3) the adoption, on 30 October 2018, of the new investment code to allow, on the one hand, the private sector to play fully its role as the engine of economic growth and, on the other, to increase the level of investment in promising and innovative sectors.

Mr President, Ladies and Gentlemen Deputies,

The development of human capital, as provided for by the PNDES, is the means for the government to develop the social sectors of education and health so as to make them, in the long term, factors of GDP growth. Indeed, a population in good health and well trained has a potential of more productive individuals, capable of adapting to technological innovations and to changes over time. That is why the government's policy aimed at implementing the PNDES insists on the harmonious development of our health system.

In this field and with a view to accelerating the demographic transition, the government has: 1) pursued the construction of health infrastructure across the whole national territory; 2) improved the service provision of health structures through the strengthening of technical facilities. This was the case with the acquisition of dialysis units for the Souro Sanou and Tengandogo University Hospital Centres (CHU); 3) brought 270 health facilities up to Health and Social Promotion Centre (CSPS) standard out of a total of 304, that is 88.8%; and 4) transformed 30 CSPS in rural commune capitals into medical centres.

Likewise, the government is working to complete very soon the projects under way. These concern the transformation of 32 other CSPS into medical centres, the opening of the Specialised Institute of Traditional Medicine and Integrated Care of Ouagadougou, 98% completed, and finally the completion of the Ouagadougou cancer treatment centre construction project, executed to the tune of 57%, whose radiotherapy component should be functional within 14 months.

Access to health services has also been facilitated thanks to a vigorous policy of recruitment, training and deployment of personnel with a view to improving the ratio of number of inhabitants per doctor so as to come closer to WHO norms.

In terms of prospects, it is envisaged for the year 2019 that construction will start on the new Bobo-Dioulasso University Hospital Centre and on the Dialysis Unit of the Ouahigouya University Hospital Centre.

Mr President, Honourable Deputies,

The state of health of the population also depends on its access to drinking water and to the sanitation of its living environment. In pursuit of the objective of zero water drudgery, the government has multiplied the mobilisation of water resources. The volume of surface water was increased in 2018 to reach 6,143 million cubic metres thanks to the construction of 11 new dams and the rehabilitation of 17 others. We are pursuing the village hydraulics and simplified drinking water supply (AEPS) programme across the whole territory through the drilling of boreholes.

With the completion of important water treatment and drinking water supply works in rural and urban areas, we have, from 2017 to 2018, increased ONEA's water storage capacity by 6,450 cubic metres and raised the national drinking water access rate to 74% in 2018.

As regards the sanitation of the living environment, the Government has undertaken efforts concerning the treatment of wastewater and excreta, raising the sanitation rate from 18% in 2015 to about 22% in 2018, with the objective of reaching 34% in 2020.

In the field of housing, I shall limit myself to mentioning two major actions undertaken by the government, namely: 1) the construction, in 2018, of 1,712 social and economic dwellings and the implementation of the investment programme for the benefit of the diaspora within the framework of the 40,000 housing programme; 2) the start of development and servicing operations in rural communes.

But I would specify that the government is pursuing its efforts for the drawing up of city planning and management documents, the development of cities, notably the subdivision operation of 80 rural commune capitals, the conduct of the programme of 40,000 social and economic dwellings, as well as the clearing of urban land liabilities in accordance with Parliament's recommendations.

Mr President, Ladies and Gentlemen Deputies,

In matters of education and training, the government, in accordance with the orientations of the PNDES, pursued the objective of increasing provision at all levels of education while improving quality. It pursued this objective in 2018 in a particularly difficult context marked by social unrest in the world of education, but above all by the insecurity which caused, in the regions of the country most affected by terrorist attacks, the closure of numerous schools and the destruction of much educational infrastructure and teaching material.

To face this situation, the government took measures to regroup the pupils of the examination classes of the closed schools, in order to provide them with support courses and to organise a special examination.

With a concern to increase educational provision by diversifying fields of training, the government acted on the two levels of the construction of establishments and the training of teaching staff. It placed particular emphasis on the development of technical and vocational education through the launch of the construction of 6 science lycees, 2 technical lycees, 5 vocational lycees and 5 Technical and Vocational Teaching and Training Centres (CEFTP). It recruited and placed in internships 200 students destined for technical and vocational teaching, 163 of them in Tunisia.

Within the framework of the reform of the education system, the government has begun the piloting of new curricula in 6 regions. The strengthening of higher education and research aims to place it at the heart of our development strategies. This is a challenge to be met. We are working first to develop them, thus to improve their accessibility and to increase their quality both pedagogically and in the provision of social services. To this end, the Government has chosen to combine the creation of Polytechnic University Centres (CUP) in the regions with that of the Virtual University, which requires the establishment of open digital spaces. The development of the university map was logically accompanied by the recruitment of one hundred teachers and of 89 temporary teaching and research assistants, and the construction of lecture theatres of 1,000 and 1,500 seats to make the Ouaga II University site functional.

The promotion of research and innovation was not left out in the conduct of government action. At this level, the most important achievements in 2018 include, among others: 1) the strengthening of the capacities of the National Fund for Scientific Research and Innovation, which financed 60 research projects; 2) the recruitment of 37 researchers; and 3) the conduct of preparatory studies for the establishment of structuring projects in the research and innovation sector such as technology parks in ICT, in renewable energy and in agri-food technology.

Mr President, Honourable Deputies,

One of the major objectives of government policy is to fight unemployment and underemployment by facilitating access for all to quality jobs and to social protection, to reduce social and gender inequalities, and to promote women as dynamic actors of development.
